Hi, I suffer from social anxiety and have a hard time talking to people and being sociable. However, once I get really comfortable around people I'm the exact opposite. I can normally hold a conversation with someone on a first date, but I have to really try at it. Anyways, I recently went on a date with a girl. This date was the first time we meet in person but we have texted each other a little back and forth before hand. Now, here's the problem. She's like me...but probably even worse. It was extremely hard to keep a conversation going at all and I was really really trying my hardest. I'd try to set up dialog so that she could respond by asking a question and continuing the conversation, for example: I'd ask, "Are you doing anything cool for memorial day weekend?" and her response would be "no not really". Short simple answers for basically everything, and not even returning the question back to me. Afterwards, she said she had a great time and would like to go out again. We have texted and snapchatted since the date and she was saying she thinks she acts too awkward. I guess my question is if I go on another date with her what do we do? I've exhausted hours worth of small talk/conversation material within the first date and I haven't found any connection yet simply because we're both very reserved, especially her. Do you guys have any date ideas to help us get more comfortable around each other? Now I know how people probably feel around me, lol.
I(M19) went on a date with a very attractive, but socially awkward girl (F17). I need help talking to her.

Do something that doesn't rely on making conversation, like mini golf or bowling. Bowling is good because you are constantly walking past each other taking your turn; you are given a brief window where you could say something if you wanted, but there isn't really time (or pressure) to be chatty.

If neither of you are comfortable with small talk, why bother with it? In the words of Mia Wallace, "Why do we feel it's necessary to yak about bullshit in order to be comfortable?... That's when you know you've found somebody special. When you can just shut the fuck up for a minute and comfortably enjoy the silence."

Ask more open questions. If your conversation starter can be answered with a yes or no, then there won't be very much to say. But if you ask something like 'what's the last movie you saw in theaters,' then you can follow up with 'how did you like it, do you like that actor/director/franchise.' You'll start to have a dialogue and can learn more about each other.

Start to collect conversation ideas now. Think up some stories about fun and impressive things you've done, interesting people you've met, places you've been, and ideas that interest you. Don't be afraid to disagree, but avoid become argumentative.
A lot of great general answers here. Specifically for conversation, don't ask questions in a way that make yes or no acceptable answers.

1) Get to know her. Favorite color and why. Favorite animal and why. Childhood scars and how she got them. Look at a large list of questionares and take the intersting ones. I used to love asking people I just met that so I could judge them by their answers. People always had a great time answering and thought I was very interested in them.

2) Plan activities. If you are hiking, biking, rock climbing, taking a walk while you eat a treat like ice cream, or other active activities then silence isn't so awkward since you've something to focus on. You can also do fun things like graffiti (you can do it with chalk it you don't want to break the law), swimming at a waterfall, or junk like that.

3) Don't talk. You can bond playing videogames, watching movies, dancing at clubs, or other things where talking isn't required.

4) Talk online. People tend to be much more open online because it's not intimidating. You can always stay online buddies for a week or two and once you guys have a few serious conversations give real life another shot. The bonding I've done with people online vs. real life is crazy different.

Ultimately, you guys just want to try and get to a comfortable place. It just takes time, even if it involves a few awkward outings.

Really anything that can take attention away from the conversation is great. Basically you want small distractions you can talk about. Games are great. But you could also go to a museum or art exhibit. It allows both of you to comment on what you see and talk about short topics.

The point is for both of you to relax around each other, then conversation can find it's natural balance and flow.
